event: US weekly initial jobless claims (week ending Nov 7)
why: A softer labor market raises rate-cut odds, which can weaken the dollar and lift metals.

event: Fed speakers: Hammack (8:00am CT), Goolsbee at Yahoo Finance Invest (Chicago Fed lists 10:15am CT), Daly (12:10pm CT), Williams panel (5:30pm CT)
why: Rate-path hints move the dollar and with it copper, aluminum and gold.

event: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report (moved from Wednesday for Veterans Day)
why: Oil and diesel moves feed into freight costs and broad commodity sentiment.

event: US Producer Price Index (October)
why: Hot producer inflation can push rate-cut hopes back and firm the dollar.

event: US Steel and United Steelworkers resume contract talks
why: A strike threat at US Steel would affect flat-rolled supply and mill scrap buying.

event: Japan Q3 (Jul-Sep) GDP, first preliminary estimate
why: Japan is a big steel and metals economy, so a weak print can dent Asian demand sentiment.

event: China October data: home prices (7:30pm CT), then industrial output, retail sales, fixed-asset and property investment (8:00pm CT)
why: China is the largest buyer of copper and steel, so these numbers often set the tone for Monday trading.
source: National Bureau of Statistics of China, 2026 release calendar

event: NY Fed Empire State Manufacturing Index (November)
why: This is the first factory read of the month and hints at US metal-consuming activity.

event: Nucor weekly Consumer Spot Price (CSP) for hot-rolled coil
why: Nucor has raised HRC 15 weeks running ($1,280/st as of Nov 2), which supports prime and shred scrap pricing.

event: AISI weekly raw steel production (week ending Nov 14)
why: Mill utilization (77.0% for the week ending Nov 7) is a direct read on ferrous scrap demand.

event: Last trading day of Shanghai's November copper contract (delivery Nov 17-18)
why: China's spot copper market is expected to stay tight until delivery, supporting prices.

event: US advance retail sales (October) and import/export prices (October)
why: Consumer strength and import inflation shape the Fed outlook and demand for autos and appliances.
source: U.S. Census Bureau; U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics

event: Fed industrial production and capacity utilization (October)
why: Manufacturing output, including primary metals and autos, tracks scrap generation and consumption.

event: NAHB Housing Market Index (November)
why: Builder confidence signals demand for copper wire, pipe, rebar and aluminum.

event: US housing starts and building permits (October)
why: Construction activity drives copper and steel use in homes.

event: FOMC minutes (Oct 27-28 meeting)
why: The tone on future cuts can swing the dollar and metals late in the session.

event: APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen; Trump says he expects to meet Xi (exact time not announced)
why: Tariff and trade-truce headlines (the truce runs to January) can jolt copper, aluminum and steel.

event: US jobless claims and Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Index (November); Fed's Hammack speaks 7:50am CT
why: Labor and regional factory data, including prices paid, feed rate expectations and metals demand views.

event: China Loan Prime Rate announcement (PBoC, November)
why: A surprise cut would be read as stimulus for Chinese construction and metals demand.

event: University of Michigan consumer sentiment, final (November)
why: Inflation expectations in the survey can move rate bets and the dollar.
